skill.name: elixir-pro
skill.description: Guides Elixir development with OTP supervision, Phoenix LiveView, Ecto, concurrency, testing, Dialyzer, benchmarking, and BEAM performance practices.
skill.summary: Provides expert Elixir guidance for OTP, Phoenix, Ecto, concurrency, testing, and BEAM optimization.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive caused by Markdown backticks around a file path in SKILL.md. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or unsafe execution behavior was found in the reviewed file.

static_findings.snippet: - If detailed examples are required, open `resources/implementation-playbook.md`.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 26 uses Markdown backticks to format a referenced file path, not Ruby or shell command execution. The skill is prompt-only and contains no executable code.

content.value_statement: Elixir teams need clear guidance for OTP, Phoenix, concurrency, testing, and BEAM performance work. This skill directs Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to produce idiomatic designs, reviews, and implementation plans.
actual_capabilities: Guides OTP design with GenServer, Supervisor, and Application patterns.
Supports Phoenix and LiveView architecture decisions for real-time features.
Advises on Ecto changesets, contexts, and database interaction boundaries.
Reviews concurrency designs using processes, Tasks, and fault isolation.
Plans ExUnit tests, doctests, Dialyzer specs, benchmarks, and telemetry coverage.
Provides BEAM performance guidance with profiling and bottleneck analysis.
limitations: It is a prompt-only skill and does not include runnable Elixir tooling.
It cannot execute tests, benchmarks, or Dialyzer checks by itself.
It references an implementation playbook that is not included in the package.
It depends on project context to give precise architecture recommendations.

use_cases.title: Design OTP Services
use_cases.description: Plan supervision trees, process boundaries, restart strategies, and failure handling for a production Elixir service.

use_cases.title: Review Phoenix LiveView Work
use_cases.description: Evaluate contexts, event flow, assigns, tests, and maintainability risks before merging a LiveView feature.

use_cases.title: Tune BEAM Performance
use_cases.description: Identify profiling targets, concurrency bottlenecks, telemetry gaps, and benchmark plans for scaling Elixir workloads.

prompt_templates.title: Explain an Elixir Design
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of an existing module or feature idea.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain this Elixir design in simple terms. Focus on OTP responsibilities, process boundaries, likely failure modes, and missing tests.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an OTP Feature
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate design work for a new supervised component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an OTP feature for this requirement. Include supervision structure, state ownership, message flow, restart strategy, and ExUnit coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Phoenix Change
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced review of Phoenix or LiveView implementation plans.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Phoenix change for idiomatic Elixir. Check context boundaries, LiveView state, Ecto usage, telemetry, and test gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Distributed System
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced analysis for performance and reliability concerns.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this distributed Elixir system. Recommend profiling steps, bottleneck hypotheses, clustering risks, benchmark design, and fault tolerance improvements.

output_examples.input: Design a fault-tolerant background worker for order processing.
output: Recommends a supervised worker tree with retry boundaries, telemetry events, and explicit failure handling.
Lists test scenarios for success, retry, timeout, crash recovery, and backpressure behavior.

output_examples.input: Review a Phoenix LiveView feature for maintainability.
output: Identifies context boundary concerns, assigns ownership, event flow risks, and validation responsibilities.
Suggests focused tests for LiveView interaction paths and data changes.

output_examples.input: Improve performance for a slow Elixir workload.
output: Prioritizes measurement with observer tools, recon checks, benchmarks, and telemetry signals.
Separates likely CPU, memory, database, and process mailbox bottlenecks.

best_practices: Provide module goals, supervision context, and failure expectations before asking for design advice.
Ask for tests, telemetry, and operational checks with every production recommendation.
Validate generated guidance against your project conventions and dependency versions.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for broad rewrites without sharing current process ownership and failure behavior.
Do not use generated OTP designs without reviewing restart impact and state recovery.
Do not treat performance advice as final without profiling and benchmarks.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps with Elixir architecture, OTP patterns, Phoenix LiveView, Ecto, testing, and BEAM performance planning.

faq.question: Does it run Elixir commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance only and does not include scripts or executable tooling.

faq.question: Can it review existing code?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide relevant files or summaries so it can review design, tests, and maintainability risks.

faq.question: Is it useful for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. It can explain OTP and Phoenix decisions in direct language before suggesting implementation steps.

faq.question: Can it optimize production systems?
faq.answer: It can plan profiling, benchmarking, telemetry, and bottleneck analysis, but you must run the measurements.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The package declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
